# tfutils_kubernetes_ready_wait (Resource)

On create, waits until a Kubernetes object exists and every entry of `conditions` matches its `status.conditions`, for example until a CRD is `Established` or a webhook Deployment is `Available`. Use it as a create gate in the module that needs the object, without a reference to the module that creates it, so that later changes to that module do not make this module wait. A 404 means not yet; a 401 or 403 fails at once. Apply fails with the last state when the create timeout passes. Read makes no request; the wait runs again only when the inputs or `triggers` change. Destroy does nothing.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "tfutils_kubernetes_ready_wait" "certificates_crd" {
  api_version = "apiextensions.k8s.io/v1"
  resource    = "customresourcedefinitions"
  name        = "certificates.cert-manager.io"
  conditions  = { Established = "True" }

  provider = tfutils.cluster
}

resource "kubectl_manifest" "certificate" {
  yaml_body = file("${path.module}/certificate.yaml")

  depends_on = [tfutils_kubernetes_ready_wait.certificates_crd]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `api_version` (String) `apiVersion` of the object, for example `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` or `v1`.
- `conditions` (Map of String) Condition `type` to expected `status`, for example `{ Established = "True" }`. An empty map waits only until the object exists.
- `name` (String) Name of the object.
- `resource` (String) Plural resource name, for example `customresourcedefinitions` or `deployments`.

### Optional

- `namespace` (String) Namespace of a namespaced object.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `triggers` (Map of String) Values whose change replaces the resource and runs the wait again.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) API path of the object.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
